messages:
kim_customer: Hey team — running into a weird one. When our frontend connects to the Redwood streaming endpoint via our grpc-gateway (Envoy-based) the SSE stream starts but then cuts off after ~6-12s. Hitting the API directly (no gateway) works fine and we get the full stream. Any ideas?

alex_support: Thanks for the report, kim. Can you paste the curl you used to repro and the behavior you see? Also, does the gateway translate HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 or do you terminate TLS at the gateway?

kim_customer: We terminate TLS at gateway then proxy to the Redwood API over HTTP/2. Repro curl (direct vs via gateway):

```
# direct (works)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-stream-demo"

# via gateway (fails after partial output)
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://internal-gw.example.com/proxy/redwood/streams?model=gpt-stream-demo"
```

The via-gateway one prints the initial events but then we see either a socket close or a single chunk of "data: ..." and then nothing. No 500 or 4xx returned.

alex_support: Do you see any 401/403 mid-stream or any token refresh attempts? Also, any logs from the gateway when this happens?

maria_sre: FWIW, HTTP/2 doesn't use Transfer-Encoding: chunked — proxies that translate HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 may buffer until end unless explicitly configured to flush. Envoy has a bunch of knobs for streaming passthrough.

kim_customer: No token refreshes; token lifetime is long. Gateway logs show a few entries like: 

```
[envoy] upstream response for /proxy/redwood/streams: headers_received, 200
[envoy] upstream response body buffered, connection to upstream closed by peer
[envoy] downstream stream ended: local reset
```

We also saw occasional "upstream response body buffered" messages.

alex_support: That buffering line is a red flag. Some gateways (and gRPC->HTTP/1.1 translation layers) buffer full responses by default. If the upstream (Redwood) is streaming via HTTP/2 frames, Envoy might not flush to downstream until some threshold is hit or until the stream ends.

david_eng: A few concrete things to check:
- Ensure proxy HTTP version to upstream is http2 and you use proper stream proxying, not a translation that converts to chunked HTTP/1.1.
- Turn off response buffering in NGINX-style proxies (proxy_buffering off) or enable envoy upstream flush/streaming.
- For envoy specifically: set `upstream_config.streaming_flush_interval` or use `common_http_protocol_options` with `allow_chunked_length: true` (depends on version).

alex_support: Can you try a minimal repro where the gateway just TLS-terminates and does a straight TCP/HTTP passthrough (no layer 7 buffering)? If that works it's definitely proxy buffering.

kim_customer: Quick test — toggled envoy to passthrough mode for that route (just ssl passthrough). The stream stays alive and we get full events. So sounds like buffering.

maria_sre: Another gotcha: some gRPC gateways implement an HTTP bridging path that collects the full gRPC response before converting to SSE. In those cases streaming is impossible without using gRPC server-streaming directly.

kim_customer: Hmm we are using a custom grpc-gateway layer in front of several upstreams. Is there a recommended pattern for SSE with Envoy/gRPC proxies to avoid this?

alex_support: Recommendations we give to customers:
- Prefer using an HTTP/1.1 passthrough for SSE endpoints or configure L7 proxies not to buffer responses.
- If you must translate between protocols, use a proxy that supports streaming translation (gRPC server-stream -> HTTP/1.1 chunked passthrough) and ensure flush is enabled.
- For Envoy: disable response buffering for the route, and adjust idle/flush timeouts. Also check `stream_idle_timeout` and `max_stream_duration`.

david_eng: I'll paste an envoy-ish snippet we've seen work for live passthrough:

```
# envoy route config (illustrative)
route:
  match: { prefix: "/proxy/redwood/" }
  route: { cluster: redwood_upstream }
  typed_per_filter_config:
    envoy.filters.http.buffer:
      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.buffer.v3.Buffer
      max_request_bytes: 0  # disable buffering
    envoy.filters.http.router: {}
common_http_protocol_options:
  idle_timeout: 0s
```

Not all deployments use the buffer filter; check your stack.

kim_customer: We don't have the buffer filter but hit `upstream response body buffered` anyway. Searching suggests it's the HTTP bridge / translator path.

alex_support: Also check the downstream client behavior: browsers and some fetch polyfills may treat streaming over HTTP/2 differently. For example, Chrome historically didn't fully expose streaming response bodies over fetch with HTTP/2 unless using specific APIs or enabling chunked-encoding behavior at the server. If your frontend is a browser, try a plain curl test to rule that out — you already did this which is good.

kim_customer: We do see curl repros too, so it's not just browser.

maria_sre: There are also occasional mid-stream 401/403 when auth middleware attempts to validate tokens asynchronously and returns an auth error that closes the stream. That would show a 401, though. Since you don't see that, it's less likely.

kim_customer: One more weird thing: sometimes the stream stops with a small chunk that appears to be a half-event, like the last event is truncated mid-line. Our server logs show: `write: broken pipe` around the same time. Looks like client connection closed.

alex_support: Broken pipe at the application usually means the downstream closed (or proxy shot the connection). Given passtrough works, gateway is the culprit. Two practical fixes:
1) Switch the route to TCP passthrough for SSE endpoints.
2) If you must keep L7, configure gateway to disable buffering + enable flush buckets. For nginx example: `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_cache off;`

kim_customer: We implemented proxy_buffering off and the stream improved but still saw occasional truncation under load. Any other suggestions?
alex_support: Under load maybe upstream flush thresholds or flow-control windows come into play. For HTTP/2 you also need to tune SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE and SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE if proxies are interfering. Also confirm there are no intermediate load balancers that terminate and re-establish connections — extra hops can add buffering.

david_eng: If you can share a small tcpdump of the upstream conversation (redacted tokens) we can check whether Envoy is receiving the frames from Redwood and then holding them, or whether Redwood is closing. From your earlier note, upstream said "connection to upstream closed by peer" — that might mean Redwood closed after finishing sending (expected) but Envoy buffered and then locally reset when it hit some internal limit.

kim_customer: We'll capture pcap and send. One more thought: any Redwood-side settings that could cause mid-stream 401s or billing rejections? We had a billing incident once where tokens were invalidated mid-request.

alex_support: We don't revoke tokens mid-request normally. If we see auth issues they'd show up as 401/403 in the stream. Billing throttles manifest as 429 rate-limit headers or explicit errors in stream events, not silent disconnects.

maria_sre: Also check keepalive/idle timeouts on the gateway. Some gateways close idle streams after a threshold if no bytes are sent for a while — so if your model generation has pauses (thinking delays) the gateway might interpret it as idle and close it. Configure `stream_idle_timeout` to a higher value.

kim_customer: Good call — the model pauses then emits tokens, so we did see gaps. Increasing stream timeout plus disabling buffering made it stable in our staging runs.

alex_support: Great. To summarize action items we observed and recommended:
- Reproduce with curl to rule out browser client issues.
- Enable passthrough for SSE endpoints where possible.
- Disable response buffering in envoy/nginx/gateway and enable flush/flush-buckets.
- Increase stream idle timeout to account for model thinking pauses.
- If translating gRPC -> SSE, verify translation is streaming-capable (not full-buffering).
- If problems persist, provide pcaps and gateway logs and we'll inspect on our side.

kim_customer: Follow-up: after the two config changes (proxy_buffering off + stream_idle_timeout increased from 15s to 90s) the streams are stable in staging and prod so far. Thanks.

alex_support: Awesome — glad that helped. We'll keep this thread for a day to see if anything else pops up. If you can share the pcap/logs from the original repro we can add an upstream note to our docs about common Envoy/gateway configs for SSE.

deploy-bot: Ticket #SR-9876 updated: customer reported streaming failures via gateway; status -> monitoring.

ingress-gw-bot: Note: envoy cluster redwood_upstream had `upstream_response_buffering` event at 2026-02-25T14:07:02Z in previous release; new config applied for route /proxy/redwood/ on 2026-02-25T14:20:11Z.

kim_customer: Will attach pcaps and logs here in the next 24h. Thanks everyone :pray:
